content.text:
The proposal summary page is written to `src/views/GeneratedSummary.tsx` as `export default function GeneratedSummary()` with no props. All the data is in that file. I couldn't run any commands, so the typecheck, lint, token check and tests haven't been run.

**What's on the page:**
- **Header:** proposal P-2077, prepared November 12, 2026, with a "Ready to sign" badge. Below that, Maria Okafor, 77 Juniper Bend, Lakeport, prepared by Brightline Home Solar.
- **Two headline cards:**
  - The monthly payment of $149.00, with 6.49% APR and 240 months (20 years) on the same line, after the $2,000 down payment.
  - Estimated savings of $65,080 over 25 years ($1,785 the first year), marked "Estimated", with the assumptions listed underneath.
- **Your system:** 18 × 410 W panels, 7.38 kW, one microinverter per panel, an estimated 11,900 kWh a year.
- **Price:** the three line items, a $22,000 total, the $2,000 down payment and $20,000 financed.
- **Loan terms:** the amount financed, the monthly payment and the $35,760 total of 240 payments.
- **A closing note** that savings are estimates and not guaranteed.

**How the numbers are produced:** I store only the inputs (line items, down payment, APR, term, panel count and wattage, production, rate and rate increase). The page works out the totals, the payment and the savings from those, using the project's own loan and savings helpers. I checked the results against your figures and they all match: 7.38 kW, $22,000, $20,000, $149.00, $35,760, $1,785 and about $65,080. Because nothing is typed in twice, the figures can't get out of step if someone edits the data later.

**Things you might not expect:**
- **Two lines you didn't give me:** in the loan card I added "Interest over the loan" ($15,760) and "Total paid, including down payment" ($37,760). They come straight from your numbers and show the full cost of financing next to the savings estimate. Delete those two rows if you'd rather leave them out.
- **The savings estimate doesn't account for panels producing a little less each year,** because your figures don't either. Real savings could come out somewhat lower than $65,080.
- **No sign button:** the page only shows the "Ready to sign" status. A button needs something to do when clicked, and the page has no way to receive that without props. Tell me how signing works in your app and I can add it.

The page uses only the project's existing components and color tokens, with no hard-coded colors or pixel sizes.
